newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY

- Premier Li Peng outlines China's energy policy, expounding on development of the energy industry, conservation policies and the relationship between energy development and sustainable economic growth.

- Full text of an interview with head of the National People's Congress Qiao Shi, who speaks on China's economic development, democratic and legal development, the return of Hong Kong, environmental protection and international relations.
- A Chinese navy fleet returns to southern China's Guangdong province after a goodwill visit to the United States, Mexico, Peru and Chile.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- A nationwide tax probe ferrets out 22 billion yuan in irregular funds.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- The State Council issues details rules for supply and marketing cooperatives to conduct foreign trade.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- Eastern Zhejiang province aims to earn $1.26 billion in silk exports in the year 2000.
MARKET DAILY
- Heavy oil prices in Guangdong province fall on rising imports.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- Premier Li Peng says China plans coal output of 1.45 billion tonnes in the year 2000, with exports of 50 million tonnes.
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- State-owned feed firms in Sichuan province have formed an alliance to reverse mounting losses and compete with foreign and private companies.
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- Shanghai tax authorities are aiming to collect 15.06 billion yuan in foreign-related taxes in 1997. Officials say half the foreign firms in Shanghai evade taxes.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Japan's Nippon Electronics Corporation (NEC) signs a contract for a one billion dollar chip plant, the largest Sino-Japanese joint venture in the electronics industry.
CHINA DAILY
- The China Commodity Market Information Network, the first large-scale commodity information computer network in the country, officially opens in Beijing.
- China and the South Korea hold the third round of consular talks in Beijing, discussing problems in consular relations.
